name: GCW World Championship
epitaph: The top belt of a federation that changed it six times in eight months without a repeat champion, and did not leave the name of one of them behind.
notes: Declared in the hobby's own directory of the five e-mail wrestling leagues, 13 June 1993: “This league recognises four singles and four tag team titles in the following divisions: World, Pan American, Euro-African, and Austral-Asian” (promotions/rspw/archive/a-comprehensive-guide-to-e-mail-wrestling-1993-06-13.html). That sentence is the whole of what is known about the belt. NO REIGN IS RECORDED, and none is owed: no document in the held record names a holder of it, on any date. The federation's own posts do not survive anywhere in the held record, so nothing further about this belt is likely to. The same entry counts the singles scene as the less stable of the two: “there have been six World champions in eight months with no repeats.” Six reigns are therefore known to have happened, and not one of the six champions is named.

name: GCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The federation's senior tag belts, and by its own writer's account the most stable thing in it: one team held them for all but seven days of the first six months. Which team is not recorded anywhere.
notes: Declared in the hobby's own directory of the five e-mail wrestling leagues, 13 June 1993: “This league recognises four singles and four tag team titles in the following divisions: World, Pan American, Euro-African, and Austral-Asian” (promotions/rspw/archive/a-comprehensive-guide-to-e-mail-wrestling-1993-06-13.html). That sentence is the whole of what is known about the belt. NO REIGN IS RECORDED, and none is owed: no document in the held record names a holder of it, on any date. The federation's own posts do not survive anywhere in the held record, so nothing further about this belt is likely to. The same entry counts the tag scene as “VERY stable”: “one team held the World tag title for all of the first six months, with the brief exception of seven days.” That reign, and the seven-day one inside it, are known to have happened, and neither team is named.
